text:
maria: Quick readout from this morning's mini-profiling run — host-side parse + tokenization looks responsible for ~11.8% median tail on 128-token requests (p95 ~17%).
jamal: Can you paste the flame or top stacks?
maria: Pasted top stacks below, stripped for noise. main hotspots: parse_request -> read_frames -> grpc_unmarshal -> tokenize_buffer.
maría: (typo, real name is maria) sorry ignore
ethan: interesting — grpc_unmarshal is a small portion, most time is in tokenize_buffer re-allocs and utf8 normalization.
carla: did you run with minibatching on/off? kernel selection could be interacting with batch size hints.
maria: Ran two passes: batching=auto and batching=1 (no batching). auto had slightly better overall throughput but host overhead % increased for small requests.
jamal: numbers?
maria: with batching=auto: median host parse time = 1.2ms, model time = 8.9ms. batching=1: host parse = 0.9ms, model = 9.1ms. But p95 host parse jumps to 2.1ms in auto case.
ethan: suggests batching heuristic is coalescing tiny requests into a bundle which increases host-side preproc jitter when fragments arrive interleaved. The kernel selector then picks a lower-cost kernel assuming smoothed sequences.
carla: could be KV cache thrash too — merged streams create more KV lookups per host-side parse. Any kvcache counters?
maria: kvcache hits dropped 3% during the run; eviction spikes aligned with the p95 host parse events.
infra-bot: deploy-log: started canary run at 1755004000, routing profile: 60% canary.
jamal: Another data point from packet traces: several requests had framing that split tokens across chunks causing extra memcpy in tokenize_buffer.
ethan: two actionable items: 1) make tokenize_buffer avoid realloc on small increments (use pre-reserve or slab allocator), 2) add an early-flat-path for already-utf8-normalized strings to skip normalization.
carla: also propose adjusting batching heuristic: prefer flushing micro-batches when host preproc backlog > X ms to avoid tail amplification.
maria: I prototyped pre-reserve: prealloc reduces median tokenize_buffer time from 0.45ms -> 0.17ms in microbench. p95 improved ~30%.
jamal: nice. For the flatten path, how detect normalized input cheaply? fast isascii check + range checks?
ethan: cheap heuristic: if bytes pass an ascii-only fast-scan, skip normalization. Add a metric to watch false-negatives.
carla: On KV side, propose a per-routing-window token affinity: keep same requester's shards mapped to same kvcache shard for short windows to reduce cross-shard lookups. Might reduce eviction churn.
maria: agree, simulated affinity lowered eviction spikes by 40% in test harness. Needs careful TTL and balancing.
jamal: let's be conscious of HTTP/gRPC overhead too — grpc writev batching is fine but http/1.1 smallwrites were killing us on edge. Any traffic mix numbers?
maria: canary was 70% grpc, 30% http1. http1 p95 host parse is ~2.8ms vs grpc ~1.9ms; parsing chunked bodies and header overhead are the suspects.
ethan: short-term: enable keepalive + pipeline hints and combine small header fragments. Longer-term: move to http/2 for those routes or add an ingress-side coalescing proxy.
carla: update runbook: 1) merge tokenize pre-reserve patch (maria) 2) add ascii-fastpath + metric (ethan) 3) tweak batching heuristic to flush micro-batches when preproc backlog > 1.5ms (jamal) 4) enable routing affinity experiment for KV in canary (carla) 5) ingress coalescing flag for http1 routes (infra).
maria: I'll open PRs for (1) and (2) today, include bench numbers and microtrace.
jamal: I'll prototype batching flush change as a config flag so we can A/B.
carla: I'll add affinity toggle and an observability dashboard for eviction spikes.
infra-bot: ticket created: PERF-7682 "host parse tail - micro-optimizations" assigned to maria,jamal,carla.
maria: one more note — when we push pre-reserve, watch memory utilization on tiny containers; we pre-alloc ~2-4KB per request handle. On density nodes this could add up. Add cap param.
ethan: good call. Use slab pooling with an upper cap per-worker and a recycle window.
jamal: ok, action items logged. will follow-up with microbench harness results by EOD. :thumbsup:
carla: thanks team. If we get p95 host parse under 1.2ms we should see ~6-8% tail improvement overall.
maria: optimistic but reasonable. will report back.
